==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|doctour||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:doctour|tree=1}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*deḱ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|doctor}}, {{m|enm|doctour||an expert, authority on a subject}}, from {{der|en|xno|doctour}}, from {{der|en|la|doctor||teacher}}, from {{m|la|doceō||to teach}}. Displaced native {{cog|enm|lerare||doctor, teacher}} (from {{cog|enm|leren||to teach, instruct}} from {{cog|ang|læran|lǣran, lēran|to teach, instruct, guide}}, compare {{cog|ang|lārēow||teacher, master}}). Displaced {{cog|ang|lǣċe||doctor, physician}}.

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q39631}} A [[physician]]; a [[member]] of the [[medical]] [[profession]]; one who is [[train]]ed and [[license]]d to [[heal]] the [[sick]] or [[injure]]d. The final [[examination]] and [[qualification]] may [[award]] a doctor [[degree]] in which case the [[post-nominal]] letters are [[w: Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine|DO]], [[DPM]], [[w:Doctor of Medicine|MD]], [[DMD]], or [[DDS]] in the [[US]], or [[MBBS]] or [[BDS]] in the [[UK]]. <!--Encyclopedic info: In the UK the qualifying exam is a first degree and the letters are [[MBBS]] or [[MBChB]]. (Usually refers to a [[general practitioner]], as others are referred to by their [[specialty|specialties]].)-->
#: {{syn|en|physician<id:Q39631>|Thesaurus:physician}}
#: {{hyper|en|person#Noun}}
#: {{ux|en|If you still feel unwell tomorrow, see your '''doctor'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Cymbeline |V|v|passage=By medicine life may be prolonged, yet death / Will seize the '''doctor''' too.}}
# A person who has attained a [[doctorate]], such as a [[Ph.D.]] or [[Th.D.]] or one of many other [[terminal degree]]s conferred by a [[college]] or [[university]].
# A [[veterinarian]]; a medical [[practitioner]] who treats non-human [[animal]]s.
# {{n-g|A [[nickname]] for a person who has special knowledge or talents to manipulate or arrange transactions.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[teacher]]; one skilled in a [[profession]] or a branch of knowledge; a learned man.
#* {{RQ:Latimer Lords Prayer|chapter=[The First Sermon]|folio=5|verso=1|passage=So from that tyme forwarde I began to ſmell the word of god, and forſoke the ſchole '''doctors''' and ſuch foolries.}}
#* {{RQ:Bacon Essayes|chapter=Of Goodness and Goodness of Nature|passage=one of the '''doctors''' of Italy, Nicholas Macciavel}}
# {{lb|en|dated}} Any [[mechanical]] [[contrivance]] intended to remedy a difficulty or serve some purpose in an [[exigency]].
#: ''the '''doctor''' of a calico-printing machine, which is a knife to remove superfluous colouring matter''
#: ''the '''doctor''', or auxiliary engine, also called "donkey engine"''
# A fish, the [[friar skate]].
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[witch doctor]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1937|year_published=1947|author={{w|Ion L. Idriess}}|title={{w|Over the Range (Idriess book)|Over the Range}}|publisher={{w|Angus and Robertson}}|location=Sydney|page=177|passage=[T]he material operation is that the '''doctor''' would catch a certain species of lizard under particular circumstances at a particular time. He would croon over it the name of the man while gently rattling his ‘devil bones,’ thus calling up the evil spirit that follows these particular charmed bones.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete|nautical|slang}} A [[ship]]'s [[cook]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1844|author=William Robert Wilde|title=Narrative of a Voyage to Madeira, Teneriffe and Along the Shores of the Mediterranean|page=124
|passage={{...}} old Scotch Jem the boatswain, tunes his fiddle, and the '''doctor''', (ship's cook,) produces his tambourine; the men dance on deck, {{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1881|title=The United Service|volume=5|page=212
|passage=His galley is small, and, microscopic as it is, it is shared by his brother in misery, the ship's cook, he whom the crew familiarly know as the “'''Doctor'''.”}}

====Usage notes====
* '''[[Doctor]]''' is capitalized when used as a title:
*: '''''Doctor''' Smith''
* In the UK and Commonwealth (except Canada), a surgeon (including a dental or veterinary surgeon) is commonly addressed as Mr./Ms./Mrs. rather than Doctor.

====Synonyms====

* {{sense|veterinarian}} {{l|en|vet}}, {{l|en|veterinarian}}, {{l|en|veterinary}}, {{l|en|veterinary surgeon}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To act as a medical [[#Noun|doctor]] to.
#: {{ux|en|Her children '''doctored''' her back to health.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|humorous}} To act as a medical [[#Noun|doctor]].
#* '''2017''', "Do No Harm", season 8, episode 2 of ''{{w|Adventure Time}}''
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To make (someone) into an (academic) [[#Noun|doctor]]; to [[confer]] a [[doctorate]] upon.
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[physically]] [[alter]] ([[medically]] or [[surgically]]) a living being in order to change [[growth]] or [[behavior]].
#: {{ux|en|They '''doctored''' their apple trees by vigorous pruning, and now the dwarfed trees are easier to pick.}}
#: {{ux|en|We may legally '''doctor''' a pet to reduce its libido.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[genetically]] [[alter]] an [[extant]] [[species]].
#: {{ux|en|Mendel's discoveries showed how the evolution of a species may be '''doctored'''.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|figurative}} To [[alter]] or make [[obscure]], as with the intention to [[deceive]], especially a [[document]].
#: {{ux|en|To '''doctor''' the signature of an [[instrument]] with intent to defraud is an example of [[forgery]].}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|author=Edward Helmore|title=How a picture came to symbolize the Prince Andrew sexual abuse case|date=2022-02-15|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2022/feb/15/virginia-giuffre-prince-andrew-picture-settlement-lawsuit|passage=That picture – the one that Andrew claimed on BBC’s Newsnight might have been '''doctored''', since he had “no recollection” of then or ever meeting Giuffre at Tramp nightclub in London – will likely serve as both a prequel and postscript of the saga.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261023140606/https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2022/feb/15/virginia-giuffre-prince-andrew-picture-settlement-lawsuit|archivedate=23 October 2026}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=Mark Landler|title=Princess of Wales Apologizes, Saying She Edited Image|date=2024-03-11|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/03/11/world/europe/princess-kate-middleton-photo-edit-apology.html|author2=Lauren Leatherby|passage=Catherine, the Princess of Wales, apologized on Monday for '''doctoring''' a photo of her with her three children, which was recalled by several news agencies on Sunday after they determined the image had been manipulated.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250804155915/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/03/11/world/europe/princess-kate-middleton-photo-edit-apology.html|archivedate=4 August 2025}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[adulterate]], [[drug]]{{,}} or [[poison]] (drink).
#* {{RQ:Bramah Max Carrados|passage=There is no doubt that a few months ago Creake deliberately planned to poison her with some weed-killer. {{...}} The gist of it was that she had the strongest suspicion that Creake '''doctored''' a bottle of stout which he expected she would drink for her supper when she was alone.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To take [[medicine]].
